clue.text: Mother has odd need, a woman with passion to become a lady on stage

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

indicators.note: odd here means strange, so the letters that follow are put into a strange new order

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis
rage is a violent passion

explanation.surface: A mother with an unusual need and a passionate woman decide to go on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Humphries' character is the definition, 'a lady on stage'; 'odd' turns NEED plus A into EEDNA, and 'has' and 'with' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry Humphries' famous stage character was a grand dame, a lady who existed only in performance.

clue.text: Saint? Saint! You and I go all funny

indicators.note: funny means peculiar or odd, so all the preceding letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cries out at a saint while a pair of people start acting strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go all funny' reads as one phrase, but GO and ALL are fodder with SAINT, YOU and I; only 'funny' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Jesuits was canonised, so he is a saint by name and rank.

clue.text: PM not right, any number sore

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out of the surname

parts.note: Tony Blair was a British Prime Minister
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A prime minister, leaving the right wing, has any number of sores.
explanation.definitionFit: A blain is an old word for a blister or inflamed sore on the skin.

clue.text: Party in which lovely lass is injected with drug

parts.note: fine can mean lovely, as in a fine day

indicators.note: the girl's word takes in the drug, like a needle going into skin

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or lass
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A political group where a pretty girl gets jabbed with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine Gael is one of the main political parties in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Nasty delivery to put up with — Pasquale gets caught

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun is caught inside the word for tolerate

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with it
the setter is Pasquale, so he refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A setter admits he can tolerate a nasty ball bowled at him, then is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' tempts a cricket reading (C for caught), but here it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a beamer is a dangerous full toss aimed at head height, a nasty ball to receive.

clue.text: Somehow stranded? Get taxi — all die otherwise!

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters take another order

explanation.surface: Grab a cab or everyone will die, someone urges anxiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get taxi' sounds like an instruction, but 'Get' is a link; 'otherwise' reorders the six letters of the dying phrase into LELAID, and the question mark flags a whimsical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable-laid rope is made by twisting three ropes together, so it is stranded in a particular way.

clue.text: See 2
Get rid of beer! Lather about act to use the end of it in desperation?

definitions.text: act to use the end of it in desperation?

parts.note: to scrap something is to get rid of it

indicators.note: about means around, so these words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ordered to ditch the frothy beer resorts to the last of the barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'Get rid of beer!' look like one command, but the beer joins the lather: 'about' reorders those ten letters into ETHEBARREL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means using whatever is left when nothing better remains, like scraping the bottom of a cask.

clue.text: A formal procedure when sculptor's brought in rock

indicators.note: the sculptor is brought into the word for a ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a formal or ceremonial procedure
Eric Gill was an English sculptor and typeface designer

explanation.surface: A ceremony is held as a sculptor arrives with a block of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Argillite is a hard sedimentary rock formed from compacted clay.

clue.text: A character at the end? Nothing, almost frozen lifeless

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for frozen is dropped

parts.note: icy means frozen

explanation.surface: A figure at the end of things is left with nothing, nearly frozen and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Azoic describes geological eras before life appeared, so it means without living things.

clue.text: Latin is shoved into each small child — truly a dead language

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Latin is pushed inside the short form of each

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Every little one is force-fed Latin, which truly is a dead language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' and 'dead language' tempt LATIN as answer, but it is only the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Elamite was spoken in ancient Elam, in what is now Iran, and has no living speakers.

clue.text: Country eggs taken to Welsh town

indicators.note: taken to means carried to and set beside, so the eggs come after the town

parts.note: Mold is a town in north-east Wales
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Eggs are delivered to a small town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a landlocked country in eastern Europe, between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: Encouragement to perform for very little money once

definitions.meaning: a cry urging someone to go ahead and act
a small old Dutch coin, so a trifling sum

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges action; the coin was a tiny former denomination, hence very little money.

clue.text: Educational set-up gives challenge over year — then learner's given peace

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for challenge is spread over the letter for year

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
L is for learner, as on L-plates
ease is peace or comfort

explanation.surface: A course hands out a challenge across the year, then the student gets some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Day release is a scheme letting employees leave work on set days to attend college.

clue.text: Academics read up German novelist with a Dickensian character

indicators.note: in a down clue, read up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dons are university teachers
Günter Grass was the German author of The Tin Drum

explanation.surface: Scholars study a German writer alongside a character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read up' looks like studying, but turns DONS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus Snodgrass is one of the members of the Pickwick Club in Dickens' first novel.

clue.text: Ways artist can go around the side

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Roads where a painter may wander round the outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' means a sports team here: Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous London football club, and a team is often called a side.

clue.text: Party chick wings off — idle, sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
the wings of a word are its outside letters, so the first and last letters are cut

explanation.surface: At a party a young woman, lazing about drunkenly, loses her inhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings off' trims CHICK to HIC, and 'sozzled' mixes HIC with IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.

clue.text: Try prisoner first? Won't be wanted in court

indicators.note: first places the prisoner ahead of the word for try

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
tempt in an older sense means to try or test

explanation.surface: A judge suggests putting a prisoner on trial first, though he is unwelcome in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is behaviour that defies a court, so it is the last thing a judge wants.

clue.text: Hit man is wandering around in old Corinth

indicators.note: wandering around suggests moving aimlessly, so the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: An assassin roams the streets of ancient Corinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth stood on an isthmus and hosted the Isthmian Games, so the adjective describes things there.

clue.text: Checking up on girl, I may have technique to discover age!

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
dating, as in carbon dating, establishes how old something is

explanation.surface: A girl wonders whether she has a way to find out someone's age.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate is to confirm, so validating is checking that something is correct.

clue.text: Drink has cat, maybe, going under flap

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is written below the first

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
a cat is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A cat drinks and then slips beneath a flap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lappet is a small flap or fold, as of cloth on a garment or of flesh.

clue.text: In French class you look at a particular dialect

parts.note: tu is the familiar class of the French word for you
to scan is to look at closely

explanation.surface: In a French lesson a student is told to look at a regional dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan is the dialect of Tuscany, the basis of standard Italian.

clue.text: Go mad, doing a flip

indicators.note: flipping over turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy and does a somersault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun, an attempt, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab and a go are both informal words for an attempt.

clue.text: Hello — friend's drunk that bottle!

indicators.note: drunk means taken in, so the greeting goes inside the friend's word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
hi is a greeting, hello

explanation.surface: A greeting is called out as a friend downs the whole bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone drinking a bottle dry; the container reading of 'drunk' (swallowed whole) is the one that works, and 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Someone selling leftovers in shops?

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
orts are scraps of leftover food

explanation.surface: A salesman offers leftover goods in stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shops' is a verb: to shop someone is to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, which is what reporting them does.

clue.text: Stink in city when monster disappears — one in graveyard?

indicators.note: in places the word for a smell into the city, filling the gap left behind
disappears means the alien's letters vanish from the city's name

parts.note: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, England
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A city reeks once the monster has gone, leaving someone in the cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: The smell is put in the city in place of the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhumer digs up a buried body, so does that work in a cemetery.

clue.text: Have a 22 at more than one partygoer, losing little time

indicators.note: losing means the abbreviation for time is taken out

parts.note: guests are people at a party
T is short for time

explanation.surface: Several party guests try their luck, losing track of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 across is STAB, so the definition reads 'have a stab at'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to attempt it, which is what a guess is.

clue.text: Top man setting a record with food and drink

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
ham is a food
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A leader is chosen while playing a record over food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The dominant male in a group, the top dog, is called the alpha male.
